name: L'Origine du monde
material: The psychoanalyst Jacques Lacan bought L'Origine du monde in 1955 and kept it hidden behind a sliding panel painted by André Masson.
Lacan concealed the painting for decades; only intimate visitors were shown the panel slid aside.
After Lacan's death the French state accepted the painting in lieu of inheritance tax in 1995, and it entered the Musée d'Orsay.

name: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe
material: Édouard Manet submitted Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe to the 1863 Paris Salon, which rejected it.
The jury refused the work and it was shown instead at the Salon des Refusés, where crowds mocked the nude woman seated with clothed men.
Manet was attacked by critics but the scandal made him the figurehead of a new generation of painters.

name: Bal du moulin de la Galette

matrix.canonical_title: Bal du moulin de la Galette

material: Gustave Caillebotte, himself a painter, bought Bal du moulin de la Galette from Renoir and bequeathed it to the French state on his death in 1894.
The state hesitated for years to accept Caillebotte's bequest of Impressionist works, fearing scandal.
Renoir painted the dance hall outdoors in Montmartre, carrying the large canvas up the hill each day.

name: Starry Night Over the Rhône
material: Vincent van Gogh painted Starry Night Over the Rhône in Arles in 1888, working at night by gaslight with candles fixed to his hat.
He wrote to his brother Theo that he needed to paint the night sky directly rather than from memory.
The painting measures 72.5 by 92 centimetres, oil on canvas.

name: L'Église d'Auvers-sur-Oise
material: Vincent van Gogh painted the church at Auvers-sur-Oise in June 1890, weeks before he shot himself in a nearby wheatfield.
He wrote to his sister that the building appeared violet against a deep blue sky, straining to capture it quickly.
He died on 29 July 1890; the painting is among the last he completed.
